question:

each cell contains at most one chip
all chips in the same row and all chips in the same column have the same colour
any additional chip placed on the grid would violate one or more of the previous two conditions.

- If a **row** contains any chips, then **every column intersecting that row must also be monochromatic** and of the **same color** as the row.
- Similarly, if a **column** contains any chips, then **every row intersecting that column must also be monochromatic** and of the **same color** as the column.

This leads to the following:

- If **any row** is white, then **every column** intersecting it must also be white.
- If **any column** is black, then **every row** intersecting it must also be black.
- Therefore, **if a row and a column are of different colors**, their intersection would have conflicting colors — which is **not allowed**.

Thus, the only way to avoid such conflicts is to have **all rows and columns of the same color**. That is:

- Either **all rows and columns are white** → the entire grid is filled with white chips.
- Or **all rows and columns are black** → the entire grid is filled with black chips.

Any other configuration (e.g., some rows white and some black) would result in **conflicting colors** in the intersection of rows and columns, violating the monochromatic condition.

---

### Counting the Valid Configurations:

- **All white chips**: Fill the entire $5 \times 5$ grid with white chips. This uses **25 white chips**.
- **All black chips**: Fill the entire $5 \times 5$ grid with black chips. This uses **25 black chips**.

These are the **only** configurations that satisfy the **maximality** condition.

---

### Conclusion:

There are **exactly two** valid configurations: one with all white chips and one with all black chips.
